name: guild
description: Continuous agent orchestration where the plugin IS a schema and a set of skills — there is no CLI. `tursodb` already executes SQL, so guild members reach the board by writing their own SQL against a guide, and the guild's rules live IN the database: CHECK constraints are the status vocabularies, VIEWS are the derived rules (the cursor, the review gate, node readiness, the matcher, the board, the brief — each with ONE definition, so two members cannot get two answers), and TRIGGERS write the `event` record on every mutation. A member can forget to call a command; a member cannot bypass a trigger or a CHECK. A ticket names a required CAPABILITY rather than an agent, so adding an agent file is the whole of hiring, and it carries the file set it owns in `files` — the architect's assertion that lets a wave run concurrently in one working tree. Each requirement runs an execution graph with three gates: the plan is approved before anything is built, findings, bugs and failures are presented together as one decision after review, and the repair plan is approved before any fix is written. Between gates it can work a shift unattended, stopping at the next gate because a gate is the one decision no subagent can make. Say 'check in' to start a work session, or 'work a shift' to leave it running.
